\#\# The finding — the em dash in the jobs folder name is a trap that conceals itself  
  
\`G:\\My Drive\\01-JOBS — ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH\`. A script saved \*\*without a byte-order mark\*\* and launched with  
the \*\*old\*\* PowerShell (\`powershell.exe\` 5.1) misreads that dash and uses  
\`G:\\My Drive\\01-JOBS â€” ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH\` instead — \*\*and that folder exists on the Drive\*\*, created  
2026-08-23, holding 5 empty capsule shells.  
  
\*\*Why nothing crashes:\*\* the path is in \*\*single\*\* quotes. In double quotes the mangled text contains a  
smart quote, 5.1 throws \`Unexpected token\`, and the script dies loudly. In single quotes it is just text,  
so the script \*\*runs to completion and prints a clean success line\*\* at the wrong address. And the obvious  
guard — \*does the folder exist?\* — \*\*answers True\*\*, because the phantom is really there. Proved three  
ways with a two-line test file: 5.1+no-BOM resolves to the phantom, 5.1+BOM and pwsh-7 both resolve  
correctly, and all three report \`EXISTS: True\`.  
  
\*\*Method note:\*\* do \*\*not\*\* test this with \`Parser::ParseFile\` — it decodes BOM-less files as UTF-8 and  
returns \`PARSE-OK\`, which is not what the \`-File\` loader does. Model the loader: raw bytes →  
\`\[Text.Encoding\]::Default\` → \`ParseInput\`.  
  
\*\*Counted, not estimated: 38\*\* scripts embed that path. \*\*30 already carry the mark. 8 do not\*\* —  
\`Matter-Stage-Engine.ps1\`, \*\*\`VTS\\Build-Job-Portal.ps1\` (the Orange Tree builder)\*\*,  
\`VTS\\Build-Master-Capsule-Portal.ps1\`, \*\*\`Count-OCR-Denominator.ps1\`\*\*, \`Build-VTES-Control-Panel.ps1\`,  
\`SystemAudit\\System-Audit-01.ps1\`, \`VTS\\Retrieve-Microfilm-Order.ps1\`, and  
\*\*\`VTS\\Set-Capsule-Hashtags.ps1\` — the canonical hashtag writer last cycle used at 03:46.\*\* Run the Orange  
Tree builder or the OCR counter from the old PowerShell and it reports on \*\*5\*\* capsules instead of \*\*42\*\*  
and calls it a complete run.  
  
\*\*Honest size: landmine, not fire.\*\* No scheduled task is exposed — the only one of the 8 that is  
scheduled (\`CU-Matter-Board-4h\`) launches with \`pwsh\`. It bites only on manual or agent-initiated runs,  
which is exactly what happened at \*\*22:34 on 09-02\*\*. Nothing is lost now: the phantom's 5 files, 7,129  
bytes, are all superseded by the real ones written \*\*01:43 today\*\*, and last cycle's Groves tag fix landed  
in the \*\*real\*\* root (its newest file is \`\_TAGS.txt\` at \*\*03:46:53\*\*).

\#\# The real defect, and why it hid — \`Send()\` returning is not transmission  
  
\`C:\\AI\\system\\morning\_report.ps1\` line 163-165 (original):  
  
\`\`\`  
$mail.Send()  
$emailSent = $true  
Write-Log "Email sent to jorgev2121@gmail.com"  
\`\`\`  
  
\`MailItem.Send()\` \*\*queues to the Outbox\*\*. It transmits only if Outlook is live and performs a  
send/receive. The script logged success the instant the call returned, so the log reads:  
  
| date | log says | truth |  
|---|---|---|  
| 08-29 | \*(no send line at all)\* | COM threw — no message exists anywhere |  
| 08-30 | \*(no send line at all)\* | COM threw — no message exists anywhere |  
| 08-31 | \`Email sent to jorgev2121@gmail.com\` | \*\*stuck in the Outbox, never transmitted\*\* |  
| 09-01 | \`Email sent to jorgev2121@gmail.com\` | \*\*stuck in the Outbox, never transmitted\*\* |  
| 09-02 | \`Email sent to jorgev2121@gmail.com\` | \*\*true — transmitted 08:00:25\*\* |  
  
So the failure is \*\*intermittent, not total\*\*: it depends on whether Outlook happened to be running  
interactively when the 8 AM task fired. On 09-02 it was. On 08-31 and 09-01 it was not, and the COM  
instance released before a send/receive ever ran. On 08-29/08-30 the COM handle failed outright and the  
script silently did \`Start-Process\` on the HTML in a hidden session — a browser window nobody saw.  
  
\*\*Four of the last six days did not reach Jorge, and the log claimed three successes.\*\*  
  
\#\# EXECUTED-WITH-PROOF — the log can no longer lie  
  
Patched \`C:\\AI\\system\\morning\_report.ps1\`. After \`Send()\` it now polls every Outbox in every store for its  
own subject, up to 45 seconds, and logs one of two things:  
  
\- \`SENT-CONFIRMED: left the Outbox\` — only when the item is actually gone.  
\- \`QUEUED-NOT-TRANSMITTED: still in '\<store\>\\Outbox' after 45s\` — plus a marker file at  
 \`C:\\AI\\system\\logs\\OUTBOX-STUCK\_\<date\>.txt\` for the next desktop cycle to find. It then falls through to  
 the existing browser fallback, so Jorge sees the report on screen instead of silently receiving nothing.  
  
\*\*It does not force a send/receive and it releases nothing\*\* — flushing an Outbox is an outbound send and  
that is not mine to do.  
  
\- Parse check: \*\*0 errors\*\* (\`Parser::ParseFile\`).  
\- Marker strings counted on disk: \*\*2\*\* — one of each, no duplication.

 \*(Its mtime reads 2026-05-29 because \`Copy-Item\` preserves the source timestamp — that is the age of the

 \`C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\\Documents\\Reports\\Undo\_Manifests\\Rollback\_MorningReportSendVerify\_2026-09-03\_0250.ps1\`

\#\# THE FINDING — THE PROOF-OF-DONE HOOK IS A SMOKE ALARM THAT FILES A REPORT, NOT A DOOR THAT STAYS SHUT  
  
JOB-0113 asked whether Everything Claude Code (ECC) could \*\*enforce the artifact-proof rule at the harness  
level — block a DONE claim with no artifact\*\* — and said that alone could justify adopting it. The reply filed  
at 23:56 last night answered \*\*no\*\*, correctly finding that ECC ships no such hook, and concluded \*"Jorge  
already owns the thing ECC lacks… Jorge's is better."\*  
  
\*\*I measured the thing Jorge owns. It cannot block anything, and it is disarmed twice over.\*\*  
  
| Switch | Measured | Effect |  
|---|---|---|  
| \`settings.json\` Stop-hook entry | \`"async": true\` | Fire-and-forget — the exit code is never waited on |  
| \`Verify-Claims.ps1\` line 108–109 | \`\# Exit 0 always — this hook reports, it must never block Jorge's session.\` / \`exit 0\` | Hard-coded pass, and documented as deliberate |  
  
\`Verify-Claims.ps1\` re-checks 44 live claims and \*\*REOPENS\*\* the failures — but that happens \*after\* the session  
already closed on a false DONE. \*\*Charter §1 (a receipt-only ACK closes nothing) and §2 (nothing is DONE  
without a checkable artifact) — the rules the charter itself names as the most-failed — are currently  
unenforced at the harness level.\*\*  
  
\#\# THE CORRECTION THAT CHANGES THE RECOMMENDATION  
  
Last night's reply justified its verdict with: \*"A Stop hook — the only place a close-out claim can be caught —  
\*\*structurally cannot veto\*\*."\* Its evidence was ECC's own \`hooks/README.md\` saying only PreToolUse can block.  
\*\*That is ECC describing ECC. It was generalised into a claim about Claude Code, and against the official hooks  
specification that generalisation is false.\*\*  
  
\`Stop\`, \`SubagentStop\` and \`TaskCompleted\` \*\*can all block\*\* — via exit code 2, or \`{"block": true,  
"blockReason": "..."}\`, with the reason fed back to the model. \*\*The gate the job asked for is native, already  
paid for, and costs zero tokens.\*\* The recommendation therefore is not "take one hook from ECC" — it is \*\*arm  
the hook that is already wired\*\*, which is a \`settings.json\` edit and so an owner call. Staged, not executed.

\#\# FIRST, THE FAILURE I CAUSED THIS CYCLE — I WROTE 37 DUPLICATE BLOCKS INTO A CLIENT DELIVERABLE  
  
Correcting the Plaza status report, I used \`$text -replace \[regex\]::Escape($anchor), $note\` with a  
multi-line here-string as the replacement. It did not insert once. \*\*It grew the file from 16,552 chars  
to 53,488 — roughly 37 stacked copies of the same block\*\*, visibly nested (\`\> \> \*\*SUPERSEDED\`).  
I have not established the exact mechanism and am not going to guess at one in a report.  
  
\*\*It was caught only because I asserted on size and then read the file back.\*\* The \`if ($new.Length -le  
$t.Length)\` guard I wrote passed happily — it only checks the file GREW. A runaway duplication grows too.  
  
Restored from the \`.bak-20260902\` I took before editing: \*\*16,713 bytes, byte-identical to the original,  
\`SUPERSEDED\` count 0.\*\* Then redone by line index, not regex: found the anchor at exactly one line (93),  
spliced 17 lines, verified \*\*\`SUPERSEDED\` count on disk = 1\*\* and line count 222 → 239. Final 18,248 bytes.  
  
\*\*Standing method note: never insert into a document with \`-replace\` and a here-string. Split to lines,  
assert the anchor appears EXACTLY ONCE, splice by index, then count the inserted marker on disk and  
require exactly 1.\*\* A size-grew check is not a duplication check.

file as ANSI, so the root became \`G:\\My Drive\\01-JOBS â€" ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH\` — \*\*a twin folder that  
already exists on the Drive\*\* (created 2026-09-02 00:26 by an earlier lane doing the same thing).

assertion is satisfied by writing nothing.\*\* This entry was re-written from a temp file on disk instead.

\#\# AND IT READS AS ZERO BYTES — WHICH IS NOT ITS SIZE  
  
\`\`\`  
Length : 0  
Attributes before read : 0x501620 RECALL\_ON\_DATA\_ACCESS + UNPINNED + OFFLINE  
File.ReadAllBytes() : returned OK, 0 bytes, NO EXCEPTION THROWN

It is an \*\*online-only Dropbox placeholder\*\*. The bytes are in the cloud and the client that fetches  
them is stopped.  
  
\#\#\# The rule — and it is worse than the iCloud one we already carry  
  
We know \*"the cloud file provider is not running"\* from iCloud. \*\*iCloud throws.\*\* The failure is  
loud; a sweep that hits it knows it failed.  
  
\> \*\*Dropbox does not throw. \`ReadAllBytes\` returns success and hands back an empty array.\*\* A sweep,  
\> an OCR pass, a hash, a "is this blank?" check — each gets a clean, confident, wrong answer: \*the  
\> file is empty\*. There is no exception to catch.  
\>  
\> \*\*Before calling any Dropbox file empty, blank, corrupt or zero-byte, test  
\> \`(Attributes -band 0x400000) -ne 0\` and check \`Get-Process Dropbox\`. A silent 0 with the client  
\> stopped is UNKNOWN, never EMPTY.\*\*  
  
Not a blanket blindness — most of the 289,944 files report real sizes and are hydrated locally. It  
bites the online-only subset, which is precisely the subset nobody has read recently. \*\*That includes  
the unswept 330 GB \`Transfer 07082025 gks\` root\*\*, so any future sweep of it inherits this defect.

reconcile on next start. \*\*No content written, nothing deleted, nothing moved.\*\* If the file comes

\#\# THE FINDING — THE MAILBOX IS THE WRONG PLACE TO ASK  
  
\`AP-0047\` asks Jorge to pick one of three receivables to chase, and lists \*\*OD-80\*\* first. OD-80's  
big question is: \*did Molino ever sign the \*\*$11,000\*\* proposal for 6915 W. Flagler Street, dated  
2025-07-28?\* The cheap way to answer that without troubling him is to ask the mail — was it sent,  
did anyone reply. So I asked the mail.  
  
| surface | \`Molino\` | |  
|---|---|---|  
| Gmail \`jorgev2121@gmail.com\` (connector) | \*\*4 threads, all machine-generated\*\* | 3 Dropbox transfer notices + 1 county "MU25001302 Issued" notice. Zero human correspondence. |  
| Outlook \`jorge@onlinecou.com\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
| Outlook \`Outlook Data File\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
| Outlook \`jorgev2121@gmail.com\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
| Outlook \`Archives\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
| Outlook \`Jorge@TEAMUSASALES.COM\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
| Outlook \`Online Archive - Jorge@TEAMUSASALES.COM\` | \*\*0\*\* | |  
  
\*\*A six-way zero is exactly the shape this machine has taught us to distrust, so it got a positive  
control before it got believed\*\* — same \`AdvancedSearch\`, same DASL filter, same scope, same 25-second  
settle, one term changed:  
  
| control | hits |  
|---|---|  
| \`Doral\` | \*\*434\*\* — 373 / 35 / 3 / 0 / 8 / 15 across the same six stores |  
  
The search works. The zero is real. \*\*And it is still the wrong answer\*\*, because:  
  
\`C:\\Jorge\\TEAM - PLANS PROCESSING\\2500 NW 79 AVE UNIT 178- MOLINO NURSING CARE LLC\\\` holds  
\*\*89 files, of which roughly thirty are \`.msg\`\*\* — the entire Doral job's correspondence, filed out  
of the mailbox into the job folder, exactly as the house standard says to file it.  
  
\#\# THE RULE, AND WHY IT IS NOT AN EDGE CASE  
  
\> \*\*A \`.msg\` filed to a job folder is invisible to mailbox search.\*\* Outlook's \`AdvancedSearch\`  
\> reads mounted stores only — it never reads loose \`.msg\` files, however well indexed the folder is.  
\> So \*\*every matter that was filed correctly answers "no mail" to a mailbox sweep.\*\* Before  
\> reporting a mail-based absence — \*never sent\*, \*never replied\*, \*no correspondence\* — glob the job  
\> folder for \`\*.msg\`.  
  
Two of our standing habits assume the opposite (\*ask the sent mail before you ask the owner\*; \*the  
Drafts folder is where outbound work dies\*). Both still hold for live mail. Neither holds for a  
matter that has been filed.  
  
\*\*Second blindness, separate:\*\* \`urn:schemas:httpmail:textdescription LIKE\` does not read  
\*\*attachment contents\*\*. A proposal sent as a PDF under a bland subject is invisible twice over. So  
the six-way zero means "no subject-or-body mention," which is weaker than "was never sent."  
  
\#\# WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE FOR OD-80  
  
\*\*It does not answer whether they signed.\*\* It establishes that the question cannot be answered by  
mailbox search, and that any future attempt will return a confident, wrong "no record."  
  
The proposal file itself is \*\*still not located\*\*. The 2026-08-25 payer sweep names  
\`Final\_Proposal\_Molino\_Nursing\_Care- 6915 W Flager St. .PDF\` — note the misspelling \*\*"Flager"\*\* —  
but gives no path, and it is \*\*not\*\* under \`C:\\Jorge\`, \`C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\`, \`C:\\Users\\JV\\Desktop\`  
or \`G:\\My Drive\`; all four were swept by filename this cycle. The next place to look is \*\*Dropbox\*\*,  
including the unswept 330 GB \`Transfer 07082025 gks\` root. That is machine work for a later cycle.

the Gmail store only. One of the two measures something else — a different tool, or a store mounted  
then and not now. \*\*Neither figure should be quoted until that is settled.\*\* It does not touch the

\#\# THE BUG IN MY OWN FIX — TWICE, AND THE TEST IS THE ONLY REASON I KNOW  
  
\`AP-0044\`'s defect is live; I re-read line 57 of \`Match-Orphans.ps1\` this cycle:  
  
 $rxUnitA = 'unit\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\\w{1,6})'  
  
"unit" matches inside the ordinary English plural "units", the separator group then matches  
nothing, and the capture takes the letter \*\*s\*\* — so "5 units in the building" yields a  
phantom apartment \*\*UNIT S\*\*. \`\\w\` also excludes the hyphen, so a real designator \*\*\`15-20a\`  
is truncated to \`15\`\*\* — a different apartment.  
  
My first replacement used \`\\bunits?\\b\`. Running it side by side against the old pattern  
showed \*\*two faults I would not have found by reading it:\*\*  
  
1\. \*\*It broke a case the old pattern got right.\*\* \`\\b\` between \`unit\` and \`221\` does not exist  
 — both are word characters — so \`unit221\` stopped matching. A silent regression, introduced  
 by the fix.  
2\. \*\*My test harness lied about a second case.\*\* \`Unit \#221\` appeared to fail. It does not.  
 \`\[regex\]'…'\` is case-\*\*sensitive\*\*; line 63 of the live script calls  
 \`\[regex\]::Matches($Text, $Pattern, 'IgnoreCase')\`. \*\*I was testing the pattern under  
 conditions production does not use.\*\* Had I trusted that reading, I would have "fixed" a  
 bug that was never there.  
  
The staged pattern replaces the trailing \`\\b\` with a lookahead:  
  
 $rxUnitA = '\\bunits?(?\!\[A-Za-z\])\[\\s\#:.\]\*(\[0-9\]\[0-9A-Za-z\\-\]{0,7})'  
  
| text | OLD | NEW |  
|---|---|---|  
| \`5 units in the building\` | \*\*\`s\`\*\* | — |  
| \`the units were inspected\` | \*\*\`s\`\*\* | — |  
| \`united states\` | \*\*\`ed\`\*\* | — |  
| \`unity plaza\` | \*\*\`y\`\*\* | — |  
| \`unit 15-20a water damage\` | \*\*\`15\`\*\* | \`15-20a\` |  
| \`unit221\` | \`221\` | \`221\` |  
| \`Units 301 and 302\` | \*\*\`s\`\*\* | \`301\` |  
| \`unit: 425\` | \*\*—\*\* | \`425\` |  
  
Four phantoms killed, one truncation fixed, one case the old pattern missed entirely now  
caught, and no regression. \*\*10 of 10 self-tests pass\*\*, run under the same \`IgnoreCase\` flag  
production uses.  
  
\*\*The trade-off, stated plainly because it is a real loss:\*\* alpha-only designators  
("Unit A", "Unit B") stop matching through \`$rxUnitA\`. They cannot be allowed back without  
re-creating the same bug — a lone letter after "unit" is indistinguishable from English  
("units I inspected", "units a few doors down"). \`$rxUnitB\` (\`\#nnnn\`) is untouched and still  
catches hash designators. If alpha units matter, that is Jorge's separate call, not this patch.

\#\# THE FINDING — a backup's mtime is the age of what is inside it  
  
I went looking for a missing backup. Sorted \`TO-CLOUD.md.bak-\*\` by \`LastWriteTime\`, newest first,  
and read: \*\*13:15:32\*\*. TO-CLOUD itself had been written at \*\*14:29\*\*. The obvious conclusion —  
and the wrong one — is that a lane prepended an hour ago and skipped the backup step, which is the  
one step the standing recipe says never to drop.  
  
The newest backup is \`TO-CLOUD.md.bak-20260902-1428\`. It was created at \*\*14:28:53\*\*, seven  
seconds before TO-CLOUD was rewritten. Nothing was skipped.  
  
\`Copy-Item\` \*\*preserves the source file's LastWriteTime.\*\* So a backup carries the mtime of the  
content it captured, never the moment of capture. Measured across every backup taken today:  
  
| | |  
|---|---|  
| backups taken today | 49 |  
| whose \`LastWriteTime\` is EARLIER than their own \`CreationTime\` | \*\*48\*\* |  
| the one exception | \`1257-pre-prepend\`, where source and copy times coincide |  
| typical skew | one full cycle — 15 to 70 minutes |  
| worst seen today | \`bak-20260902-1428\`: taken 14:28:53, stamped \*\*13:15:32\*\* |  
  
\*\*So \`LastWriteTime\` sorts these files by content age and \`CreationTime\` sorts them by when they  
were taken, and the two orders are not the same list.\*\* Sorted by mtime, \`0535-prenote\` (taken 05:16)  
appears \*newer\* than \`0522-preAP0036\` (taken 05:23). Read the filename stamp or \`CreationTime\`.  
Never the mtime.

The pile is 95% of the mailbox and grows about 4.8 MB per prepend. The cap is the right call.  
\*\*But the obvious way to write it is \`Where-Object LastWriteTime -lt (Get-Date).AddDays(-N)\`, and  
on these files that prunes by content age.\*\* A backup taken ninety seconds ago whose source was

\`CreationTime\` or on the \`bak-YYYYMMDD-HHMM\` stamp in the filename. Flagging it now, before the  
script is written, not after it deletes something.

\#\# THE FINDING — an approval card can outlive the thing it is about  
  
\`AP-0033\` has been on Jorge's board for 14.8 hours asking him to \*"say GO and the OCR sweep is restarted so it picks up its own fixes."\*  
  
\*\*There is no sweep to restart.\*\* It finished at \*\*04:33 this morning\*\* — \`SUMMARY.txt\` is written, and the run's own backup is literally named \`SUMMARY.txt.bak-20260902-COMPLETED-RUN\`. No \`Run-OCRSweep\` process exists: the only Python on this machine is LiteLLM on :4001 and three OCR \*search\* servers. The card's diagnosis was right when written; its \*\*ask\*\* expired while it sat there.  
  
So I asked the question the card was really standing in for: \*\*would the fix have rescued anything?\*\*  
  
| | |  
|---|---|  
| sweep denominator | 22,875 |  
| completed | 21,849 (95.5%) |  
| residue | \*\*1,026\*\* |  
| of which one single cause | \*\*843 rows / 831 distinct files\*\* |  
  
All 843 carry the identical message \`TypeError: Unsupported image format/type\` — \*\*674 \`.jpg\`, 122 \`.heic\`, 47 \`.jpeg\`\*\*. The run's own sniff file from cycle 10043 already proved these are \*\*valid images\*\*: PIL labels them \`MPO\` (iPhone HDR/burst shots that still carry a \`.jpg\` name) and \`HEIF\`. Neither label is in pytesseract's supported-format list, and \*\*pytesseract judges an image by its format label, not its pixels.\*\*  
  
\*\*The fix for exactly this was already written into \`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py\` at 17:49 on 09-01\*\* — lines 119-141 register \`pillow\_heif\` and \`convert()\` any unsupported label so it is treated as PNG. The run in flight since 16:01 could not have loaded it. That is precisely what \`AP-0033\` said. Nobody ever tested it.  
  
\*\*I tested it, read-only.\*\* 17 files sampled across all three extensions, run through the fixed reader verbatim:  
  
\*\*17 rescued. 0 still failing. \`pillow-heif\` INSTALLED.\*\*  
  
\*\*The honest half of that result:\*\* 11 of the 17 produced \*\*zero characters\*\* and the best produced 244. These are site photographs, not documents. The rescue is real, but the text yield is thin — expect meaningful text on roughly a third.

\#\# THE FINDING — a magic-byte check proves a file is a PDF, never that anything is written on it  
  
At 00:47 a lane cleared its own JOB-0110 Deliverable-2 blocker by finding \`Permit Application.pdf\` in Outlook, verifying it byte-wise as a real \`%PDF\`, and filing it to the capsule. It then wrote, correctly and honestly:  
  
\> \*"\`Permit Application.pdf\` (999 KB) is now in the capsule and has not yet been read page by page — that is the next place the answer may be, and it is a document task, not an owner task."\*  
  
\*\*It was right, and then it sat unread for twelve and a half hours.\*\* I read it.  
  
\*\*It is a blank Bal Harbour Village permit application template, Rev 1/13/25.\*\* Every field is underscores.  
  
| probe | result |  
|---|---|  
| \`is\_form\_pdf\` | \*\*0\*\* |  
| fillable widgets / with a value | \*\*0 / 0\*\* |  
| embedded images | 1 — \*\*211 × 41 px, 0.8% of the page\*\* = letterhead logo, no scan layer |  
| text | 5,431 chars, all blank-template wording |  
  
\*\*The mechanism, worth keeping:\*\* \`%PDF\` magic bytes prove a \*container\*. A 999 KB one-page PDF whose only image covers 0.8% of the page is a \*\*template\*\*, not an executed document — and no extension check, magic-byte check, or file-size check distinguishes those two. The distinguishing probe is \`is\_form\_pdf\` + widget values + \*\*image coverage as a share of the page\*\*.  
  
\*\*So Deliverable 2 is BLOCKED again.\*\* There is no executed prior application on this matter. The job order is explicit: \*"If no prior form is in the capsule, that is a BLOCKER, not a licence to improvise."\*  
  
\#\# WHAT I SHIPPED ANYWAY — Deliverable 3, answered from the blank form itself  
  
The blank form turned out to be worth more than the precedent would have been.  
  
\*\*(a) Is the GC the only signer? NO — now CITED, not asserted.\*\* The form carries \*\*two separate signature blocks, each with its own notary block\*\*: one \*\*Owner\*\* (\`Signature of Owner\` / \`Print Name\` / sworn-to / State of / County of / Notary Stamp), one \*\*Qualifier\*\* (an identical second block). \*\*Owner + qualifier, two notarisations.\*\* This board already carried "owner + qualifier, two notary blocks" as a claim; it now has the document behind it. Section 3 reads \*"Choose only One"\* across Building / Electrical / Mechanical / Plumbing / Gas / Roofing / Fire Sprinklers — so each trade is its own application signed by \*\*that trade's own qualifier\*\*, not the GC. \*\*No engineer or architect seal line is printed\*\*; sealed plans ride alongside.

\*\*(b) What can be omitted? Nothing citable — and I am reporting that rather than inventing a list.\*\* The form prints no instruction that any section may be skipped for an extension. JOB-0110 sets the bar itself: \*"An omission we cannot cite is not an omission, it is a rejection waiting to happen."\* What IS citable, and it is the substance of what he asked:

\#\# THE STREAK IS BROKEN — SIX CYCLES, NOT SEVEN  
  
The 12:44 lane wrote: \*"A warning that lives downstream of the defect cannot stop the defect."\* It was right, and it left the gap open. \*\*I read the mailbox before running step 2, so I never ran the destructive command.\*\* This is the first cycle in seven that did not put conflict markers into Jorge's live work registry.  
  
I replaced the pull with the non-destructive pair:  
  
\`\`\`  
git fetch origin claude/chaude-code-max20-kp2o46  
git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD FETCH\_HEAD  
\`\`\`  
  
\`merge-tree\` computes the merge \*\*in the object database only\*\*. No working tree write, no index write, no mtime moved, no abort needed afterwards. It named the conflict set directly:  
  
\`\`\`  
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in OPEN-ITEMS.md  
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in PASTE-LOG.md  
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in RECURRING-ISSUES.md  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*Same three files, obtained at zero cost.\*\* Every lane that ran the real pull to learn this paid two minutes of corrupted registry and five forged timestamps for information a read-only command hands over free.

\#\# WHAT I GOT WRONG  
  
At 11:56 I closed \`AP-0017\` citing \`CU-TypingShield-Guard\` — Enabled, Ready, ran 11:52:52, result 0, process live. \*\*That is the watcher over the shield, not the shield.\*\* Memory \`project\_the\_approvals\_board\_never\_retests\_a\_satisfied\_card\` carries this exact trap on this exact card, in red: a 05:45 pass published "the card's claim is false" off the same green guard and had to retract at 05:52. \*\*I reproduced the error I had been warned about, on the card the warning names.\*\*  
  
\#\# WHAT THE SUBJECT ACTUALLY IS — AND WHY BOTH EARLIER PASSES MISSED IT  
  
The 05:50 correction then searched for a shield \*\*process\*\*, an HKCU \`Run\` entry, and an AutoHotkey startup shortcut, found none, and left the card open. I re-ran that search and confirm the negatives: \*\*17 \`Run\` values, 61 startup shortcuts, zero matches, no shield process.\*\*  
  
\*\*Those negatives are meaningless, and this is the finding.\*\* \`Typing-Shield-Guard.ps1\` (dated 2026-07-30) shows there is no resident shield by design. The shield is a \*\*registry value\*\*:  
  
\`\`\`  
HKCU\\Control Panel\\Desktop\\ForegroundLockTimeout = 200000  
\`\`\`  
  
\`0\` means any application may yank focus mid-typing; \`200000\` is the shielded state. The guard re-asserts it every 15 minutes and reports drift.  
  
\*\*Measured this cycle: \`ForegroundLockTimeout = 200000\`. The shield is ON.\*\*  
  
The guard's own log, \`VerticalTray\_1\\VT4\\Logs\\Typing-Shield.log\`, independently agrees — \`OK: shield intact (ForegroundLockTimeout=200000)\` at \*\*11:07:16, 11:22:13, 11:37:18, 11:52:13\*\* today.  
  
So the card's premise ("It is switched OFF right now") is false, and its consequence ("does not come back after a reboot") is false across a \*\*real reboot at 2026-09-01 15:56:47\*\*, which happened after the card was written.  
  
\*\*Three passes, three different wrong subjects: the guard task (mine, 11:56), a process/Run key (05:50), and the card's own prose (08-31). The right subject is one registry value.\*\* The card's \`closed\_proof\` now names it, so the next lane does not re-derive this a fourth time.

\#\# WHAT I ACTUALLY SHIPPED — AP-0044  
  
The unit-extraction defect in the orphan matcher has been measured on three separate cycles (10032, 06:40 today, and now). Every cycle re-measured it and none of them could act, because \*\*it had no owner card of its own\*\* — that gap was itself the finding, recorded but never closed. It is closed now.  
  
\*\*Verified still live before I wrote anything.\*\* \`Match-Orphans.ps1\` line 57 reads, this minute:  
  
\`\`\`  
$rxUnitA = 'unit\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\\w{1,6})'  
\`\`\`  
  
Unchanged. The word \`unit\` is not boundary-anchored, so the matcher takes whatever follows it: the plural \`units\` yields apartment \*\*\`S\`\*\*, the word \`unity\` yields \*\*\`Y\`\*\*, \`unit unpermitted\` yields \*\*\`UNPERM\`\*\*. Three live job records carry invented apartments — \`TRK-2026-1265\` and \`TRK-2026-1412\` both carry \`S\`, \`TRK-2026-1355\` carries \`Y\`. Three of the four apartment hits in the current pool are phantoms, each worth +15 to a score it has not earned.  
  
\*\*Nothing is mis-filed and nothing is urgent\*\* — all three sit far below the 85 filing threshold, and the one real decision waiting on Jorge (\`TRK-2026-1442\`, \`UNIT 425\`) is a \*correct\* capture and is untouched by this. The card is marked accordingly: \*\*not\*\* push-worthy. The board went 34 → \*\*35 open, 10 urgent — urgent did not move.\*\*  
  
The second half is why it still matters: line 287 raises \`UNIT-CONFLICT\` only when document and job apartments \*\*fail\*\* to intersect. Two phantom \`S\` values intersect happily, so \*\*on condominium matters the safety catch never fires\*\*. The same line truncates a real \`15-20a\` to \`15\`, which defeats the catch a second way.  
  
\*\*The card carries the tested replacement so nobody re-derives it\*\*, and carries the \*rejected\* one so nobody re-proposes it. The 09-01 proposal \`'\\bunits?\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\[0-9\]\[\\w-\]{0,7})\\b'\` \*\*regresses\*\* — it requires a leading digit and would silently drop \`Unit A\`. The replacement on the card was tested against 12 real strings:  
  
\`\`\`  
(?i)\\bunit\\b\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\\d\[\\w\\-\]{0,9}|\[A-Za-z\]\\d\[\\w\\-\]{0,8}|\[A-Za-z\](?\!\[A-Za-z\]))  
\`\`\`  
  
The \`\\b\` straight after \`unit\` is the working part — it rejects \`units\`, \`unity\`, \`united\` and \`unit is located\` as a \*class\*, not one at a time, and keeps \`425\`, \`\#425\`, \`220\`, \`4B\`, \`A\`, \`721\`, and \`15-20a\` \*\*whole\*\*.  
  
\*\*\`AP-0044\` is NOT \`AP-0032\`.\*\* \`AP-0032\` is the \`.SEARCH.txt\` sidecar card, already satisfied and closed at 11:30. Attaching this defect to it would have force-reopened a satisfied card, and a wrong reopen sticks. Said plainly on the card itself.

\#\# 2. THE MECHANISM, NAMED AT THE LINE  
  
\`C:\\AI\\scripts\\MatterStage\\Finisher-01-Sweep.ps1\`, lines \*\*69–85\*\* and \*\*117–122\*\*.  
  
The register writes evidence as a \*\*bare filename\*\* or a \*\*short relative path\*\*. The gate resolves those against a fixed list of \*\*15 base directories\*\* (line 69) using a \*\*single-level \`Join-Path\`\*\* (line 118). There is no second level and no search:  
  
\`\`\`powershell  
foreach ($base in $ResolveBases) {  
 $try = Join-Path $base $p  
 if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $try) { $full = $try; $exists = $true; break }  
}  
\`\`\`  
  
So a file one folder below a base is invisible, and four folders below is invisible. Concretely:  
  
\- \`Documents\\Reports\\\` \*\*is\*\* a base — but the rollback script lives in \`Reports\\Undo\_Manifests\\\`, one level deeper. Miss.  
\- \`Documents\\ClaudeMemory\\\` \*\*is\*\* a base — the PNG lives in \`ClaudeMemory\\Dictation\\\`, one level deeper. Miss.  
\- \`Documents\\\` is a base — the cheat-sheet needs \`PERM-APP-PORTAL\\\` in between. Miss.  
\- The permit PDF sits \*\*four\*\* levels below any base, inside a per-job folder. Miss.  
\- \*\*\`C:\\Users\\JV\\JV-repository\\\` is not in the list at all\*\* — which is the whole of DIR-0090.  
  
Failure is silent and one-directional: it can only ever invent a miss, never hide one. That is why it has published every day without anyone catching it.

| Session | File date | Newest real entry | Dormant |  
|---|---|---|---|  
| \`a6d09a8e\` | 09-02 09:03:57 | \*\*07-26 16:23\*\* | \*\*38 days\*\* |  
| \`6bdecbb2\` | 09-02 09:05:38 | \*\*07-30 11:01\*\* | \*\*34 days\*\* |

\*\*The mechanism, read off the last line of each file:\*\* the app appends untimestamped metadata records — \`{"type":"ai-title",...}\` and \`{"type":"last-prompt",...}\`. \`3675ae6c\` ends in \`ai-title\`, \`1801a7d5\` ends in \`last-prompt\`. Neither carries a timestamp, so the file clock moves and the transcript does not.  
  
\*\*Count by file date: 13 open windows. Count by conversation: 3.\*\* A \~4× over-count. \*An mtime on a session log is housekeeping, not activity — read the newest entry inside the file.\*

\#\# THE FIND — the free folio-keyed permit service is real, and it is \*\*not an archive\*\*  
  
The 08:42 cycle proved the service exists and left two things explicitly \`\[VERIFY\]\`. Both are now measured, and one of them changes what should be built on it.  
  
\#\#\# 1. Date coverage — closed, and it is a \*\*rolling window\*\*  
  
\`\`\`  
outStatistics min/max on PermitIssuedDate, where=1=1  
 minD = 2024-09-01 maxD = 2026-08-31 non-null = 139222 of 139222  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*Exactly 24 months to yesterday, with zero null dates.\*\* The AGOL item \`6db5f56e886446df88313ca279e59120\` — "Building Permits Issued By Miami-Dade County — 2 Previous Years to Present" — carries \*\*\`modified 2026-09-02\`, today\*\*, so it refreshes about daily.  
  
\*\*The consequence nobody has stated: this window moves, so the service is deleting its own history.\*\* \`minD\` sitting precisely on 2024-09-01 is not a coverage floor, it is a cut line that advances every day. \*\*Every permit issued before 2024-09-01 has already fallen out, and today's oldest rows fall out tomorrow.\*\* It confirms the 08:42 warning that this will never answer a microfilm-era question — but it goes further: \*\*if this lane wants permit history, it has to snapshot the service now and keep accumulating.\*\* Read it live and you are permanently limited to two years; mirror it weekly and in a year you own three. That is the difference between a lookup and an asset, and it costs one scheduled task.  
  
\#\#\# 2. The folio joins with \*\*no normaliser at all\*\* — confirmed on the raw values  
  
\`\`\`  
FolioNumber PermitNumber PropertyAddress PermitIssuedDate  
3078110000331 2024070790 19600 SW 308 ST 2024-09-01  
3022040220030 2024070789 2100 NE 197 TER 2024-09-01  
3049220230280 2024070788 4381 SW 144 PL 2024-09-01  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*Length 13, digits only, no dashes — byte-identical to the master key the due-diligence method already uses.\*\* Populated on \*\*138,526 of 139,222 rows (99.5%)\*\*; 696 rows have none.  
  
This is the whole value of the source. It bypasses the address normaliser — and with it the compound-street-type failure that loses the house number, the unit regex that captures the plural "s" in "units", and the building-only key that matches the wrong condo unit. \*\*A join on this field cannot make those errors, because it never parses an address.\*\*  
  
\#\#\# 3. A scope limit that was about to be got wrong — it is \*\*not\*\* unincorporated-only  
  
The dataset title says "Issued By Miami-Dade County," which reads as unincorporated territory. \*\*The folio prefixes say otherwise.\*\* Counted by municipality code:  
  
| Prefix | Municipality | Rows |  
|---|---|---|  
| 30 | Unincorporated Miami-Dade | 112,898 |  
| 01 | City of Miami | 6,383 |  
| 02 | Miami Beach | 2,079 |  
| 06 | (municipal) | 656 |  
| 12 | (municipal) | 611 |  
| 13 | (municipal) | 298 |  
| 11 | (municipal) | 279 |  
  
\*\*81.5% unincorporated, but 25,628 rows carry municipal folios.\*\* So a lookup that returns nothing for a City of Miami property is \*\*not\*\* proof the service excludes municipalities — it may simply be a permit the city issued itself. \*\*Treat an empty result here as UNKNOWN, never as "no permits."\*\* These are county-issued permits on property inside municipal limits; the municipality's own building permits still live only on the municipal portal. This source \*\*supplements\*\* the Bal Harbour Village and Bay Harbor Islands portals — it does not replace them, and it must not be used to close a Plaza permit question.  
  
\#\#\# What this does to \`TRK-2026-9007\`  
  
That row has sat as \*\*REASSIGNED TO DESKTOP\*\* on the premise that county permit data must be scraped, and that the cloud lane's \`403 on CONNECT\` to \`miamidade.gov\` is what blocks it. \*\*For permits, the premise is dead\*\* — \`services.arcgis.com\` is a different host, needs no key, and answers a folio directly. The row should be re-scoped to the sources that genuinely require a browser, and the permit portion closed against this service. \*\*One caveat before anyone bulk-pulls: \`maxRecordCount\` is 1000, so a full mirror must page on \`resultOffset\` or it truncates silently at 1,000 rows while looking successful.\*\*  
  
\*\*Lead, not a finding:\*\* a second service of \*\*262,965 rows\*\* exists but its name ends in \`\_Test\`. Unverified, and I did not build on it.

\`JOB-0110\` and \`JOB-0112\` both landed overnight and both pulled the Bal Harbour eTRAKiT public  
portal on 2026-09-02. They contradict each other on exactly one permit:  
  
| Report | Written | Says \`BLC2024-0718\` (unit 815) is |  
|---|---|---|  
| \`EXECUTED\_JOB-0112\` | 00:28 | \*\*ISSUED 8/27/2026, expires 2/23/2027\*\* — "alive — get it finaled" |  
| \`REPLY-TO-CHAT\_JOB-0110\_...\_REISSUE-CLOCK\` | 05:35 | \*\*"READY, never issued"\*\* — grouped with \`0708\` and \`1333\` |  
  
I pulled all four myself at \*\*07:38\*\*, same public URL, no login —  
\`https://balh-trk.aspgov.com/eTRAKiT/Search/permit.aspx?activityNo=\<permit\>\`:  
  
| Permit | Unit | Status (live 07:38) | Issued | Expires |  
|---|---|---|---|---|  
| \*\*\`BLC2024-0718\`\*\* | \*\*815\*\* | \*\*ISSUED\*\* | \*\*8/27/2026\*\* | \*\*2/23/2027\*\* |  
| \`BLC2024-0708\` | 1016 | READY | \*(none)\* | 9/7/2025 |  
| \`BLC2024-1333\` | 307 | READY | \*(none)\* | 5/6/2025 |  
| \`BLC2024-0715\` | 721 | EXPIRED PERMIT | 1/15/2026 | 8/4/2026 |  
  
Each real record returned HTTP 200 at \*\*165–171 KB\*\* and carried its own \`Address: 10185 COLLINS  
AVE \<unit\>\`. The impossible control \`ZZZZ9999-0000\` returned \*\*44,321 bytes with no permit block at  
all\*\* — no Type, no Status, no address. So the four rows above are real records, not a page that  
renders the same shell for anything you hand it.  
  
\*\*\`JOB-0112\` is right and \`JOB-0110\` is wrong.\*\* \`0708\` and \`1333\` genuinely are READY-never-issued;  
\`0718\` is not, and it was swept into that group with them.

 the only Plaza/Bal Harbour permit of the set that is neither expired nor stuck at READY.

 pick it up.\* The true action is \*schedule inspections and get it finaled\* — different work,  
 different party, different clock.

 permit that \*\*is\*\* on a clock is the one filed as not having one.

 \`\`\`

\#\#\# The finding — the unit regex fires on ordinary English prose and pays +15 points for it  
  
\`Match-Orphans.ps1\` line 57 (file mtime 09-01 18:13 — the timeout fix did not touch this line):  
  
\`\`\`powershell  
$rxUnitA = 'unit\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\\w{1,6})'  
\`\`\`  
  
There is no word boundary after \`unit\`, so the pattern walks straight into the next letters of any  
longer word and captures them as a unit designator. Measured against the live 67-row pool:  
  
| Document | TRK | Score | "Unit" evidence | Real? |  
|---|---|---|---|---|  
| \`11785 SW 183 ST - Heating permit final ... Eugenia Marrero.pdf\` | TRK-2026-1265 | 53 | \`UNIT S\` | \*\*phantom\*\* |  
| \`Executive Summary PropertyShieldAI-InvestorPresentation.pdf\` | TRK-2026-1412 | 51 | \`UNIT S\` | \*\*phantom\*\* |  
| \`Best Practices for File Naming and Organizing (Stanford Libraries).txt\` | TRK-2026-1355 | 40 | \`UNIT Y\` | \*\*phantom\*\* |  
| \`memort recovery reboot for Joey 2026-03-26 911pm.txt\` | TRK-2026-1442 | 65 | \`UNIT 425\` | \*\*real\*\* |  
  
\*\*Three of the four unit hits in the pool are fabricated.\*\* \`UNIT S\` is the plural in "units";  
\`UNIT Y\` is the tail of "unity". Confirmed by direct test — the old pattern also returns \`ed\` from  
"united states" and \`is\` from "unit is located on".  
  
\*\*It is worth +15 real points each.\*\* Line 282 adds 15 whenever a document unit matches a job unit.  
For the evidence to read \`UNIT S\`, \*\*both sides must carry the phantom\*\* — the job register has  
\`S\` recorded as a unit too. The two defects meet in the middle and agree with each other. Strip the  
invented points and those three rows score \*\*38, 36 and 25\*\*, not 53, 51 and 40.  
  
This corroborates AP-0032's original claim on TRK-2026-1265 with live evidence, and adds a second  
poisoned matter, \*\*TRK-2026-1412\*\*. AP-0032 should be treated as \*\*live and measured\*\*, not stale.  
  
\*\*Nothing has been mis-filed.\*\* Every one of these is well under the 85 auto-file threshold — the  
same conservative threshold my predecessor showed at 06:22 is the only thing holding this pool back.

\#\#\# THE RULE THIS COST ME AN HOUR TO LEARN, AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING  
  
\*\*An expired permit's reissue clock does NOT run from its issue date. It runs from the portal's  
own Expiration Date — and every APPROVED inspection pushes that date forward, by a year or more.\*\*  
  
I built the table the fast way first: issue date + 180 days, off the capsule's permit history  
and the January 2026 export. \*\*That version was wrong on exactly the two permits that matter,  
and wrong in the direction that loses money:\*\*  
  
| | issued+180 (the export) | live portal | |  
|---|---|---|---|  
| \*\*Unit 220\*\* | window closed 2026-02-14, \*\*-200 days, dead\*\* | expires \*\*2026-08-16\*\*, \*\*163 left\*\* | \*\*alive\*\* |  
| \*\*Unit 721\*\* | \*\*no issued date at all\*\* | issued 2026-01-15, \*\*151 left\*\* | \*\*alive\*\* |  
  
Unit 220 was issued 2025-02-19 and does not expire until 2026-08-16 — \*\*543 days\*\* — because  
its \*\*FRAMING inspection was APPROVED 2026-02-17\*\*, restarting the clock. Unit 721 is missing  
from the export for the dullest possible reason: \*\*it was issued 2026-01-15, a week after the  
export was taken.\*\*  
  
Had I published the fast version, Jorge would have been told \*\*all nine permits were dead and  
needed full re-permitting under current code.\*\* The two live ones are the entire value of the job.  
  
\*\*Two independent confirmations that the live reading is the right one:\*\* the standing note in  
memory recorded unit 220 as expiring 2026-08-16 with \~163 days of window left, derived  
separately and long before today — it matches the portal to the day. And \`OPEN-ITEMS.md\` row  
9185 records unit 721 as lapsing 2026-08-04, which also matches. \*\*The export was the only  
source that disagreed, and it was the one I nearly published.\*\*

\#\#\# What the 831 are, and why they failed  
  
They are not damaged. The OCR engine judges an image by its PIL \*\*format label\*\*, not its pixels, and  
rejects anything outside its supported list. iPhones produce two labels outside it: \`MPO\` (HDR/burst  
shots that still carry a \`.jpg\` name) and \`HEIF\`. A magic-byte sniff of the set found \*\*zero corrupt,  
zero truncated, zero mislabelled, zero 0-byte\*\* — the exact inverse of the usual wrong-extension case.  
  
The fix is on disk. \`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py\` mtime \*\*2026-09-01 17:49:46\*\*, lines 139–140  
(\`img.format not in \_PYTESS\_FORMATS → convert("RGB")\`) plus the \`register\_heif\_opener()\` branch at 135,  
and \`pillow\_heif\` is installed. \*\*The run forked at 16:11, an hour and 38 minutes before its own fix was  
written, so it never loaded it.\*\* That is the whole cause.  
  
\#\#\# The recovery pass is staged, and it needs no new code  
  
I expected to have to write a requeue script. Reading the sweep instead: \`main()\` re-reads the  
denominator CSV and pre-filters on \`os.path.exists(sidecar\_for(path))\` before queuing anything  
(lines 193–194), and \`process()\` returns \`ALREADY\` for any path that slipped through (line 152–153).  
\*\*Re-running the same command now queues exactly the 1,026 files with no sidecar and skips all 21,849  
that have one.\*\* The recovery pass and a plain re-run are the same command.  
  
Staged as a one-click file, not started:  
  
\*\*\`C:\\Users\\JV\\Desktop\\RUN OCR RECOVERY PASS.cmd\`\*\*  
  
Double-click it and it runs. It is GREEN — reads originals, writes only new \`.SEARCH.txt\` sidecars  
beside them, never modifies/moves/renames/deletes an original, no network. Closing the window is safe at  
any point; every sidecar is flushed as it completes and re-running resumes. Expected: \*\*\~831 recovered,  
\~195 remain.\*\* I have quoted no finish time: this sweep's measured rate has varied 11-fold across  
cycles, so a duration would be invented.  
  
\*\*I did not start it myself.\*\* Starting a background process is a gated step in the charter, and the  
standing note on this run says restarting is ask-first. The run it would have collided with is now over,  
so the only thing left is the click.  
  
\*\*One trap caught while building it.\*\* The obvious launcher line is \`py -3\`. On this machine \`py -3\`  
resolves to \`C:\\Users\\JV\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Python\\Python313\\python.exe\`, which has \*\*no \`fitz\`\*\* —  
\`ModuleNotFoundError\` on the first import, and the window would have closed on a stack trace that looks  
like the sweep is broken. The sweep's interpreter is \`C:\\Program Files\\Python312\\python.exe\`; I imported  
\`fitz\` 1.27.2.3, \`pytesseract\`, \`pillow\_heif\` and \`PIL\` 12.0.0 under it to prove it, and hard-coded that  
absolute path into the launcher with a comment saying why it must not be changed back. \*\*A launcher is

\#\#\# The new thing: aborting the merge forges the timestamp that tells the next cycle to stand off  
  
A standing rule on this machine says that when an artifact is stamped \*\*inside\*\* your own cycle window,  
another lane is working the same order and you should stand off rather than collide. That rule is sound.  
\`git merge --abort\` breaks it.  
  
Measured this cycle, on tracked files only:  
  
| file | mtime after abort | my cycle window |  
|---|---|---|  
| \`OPEN-ITEMS.md\` | 04:35:28 | 04:35–04:41 |  
| \`PASTE-LOG.md\` | 04:35:28 | 04:35–04:41 |  
| \`RECURRING-ISSUES.md\` | 04:35:29 | 04:35–04:41 |  
  
\`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no\` returns \*\*empty\*\* — no tracked file is modified, the content  
is byte-identical to \`b00e1c8\`. Only the mtimes moved, because abort rewrites the working-tree copies to  
restore them.  
  
\*\*Why this matters more than it looks.\*\* \`OPEN-ITEMS.md\` is the live work registry — it is the first file  
a cycle reads to decide what to do. Every cycle that follows the ordered step 2 will conflict, abort, and  
thereby stamp the work registry with the current second. The next reader sees the ledger it is supposed to  
act on freshly touched, concludes a second lane is mid-write, and stands down from work it actually owns.  
\*\*Two correct rules, composed, produce a watcher that talks itself out of working\*\* — and it fails toward  
silence, which is the direction nobody audits. I nearly did exactly this: I read the 04:35:28 stamp on  
\`OPEN-ITEMS.md\` as another lane before I noticed it was my own abort, one second after my own command.  
  
\*\*How to tell them apart, cheaply:\*\* a real concurrent write changes content, an abort only changes the  
mtime. Run \`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no\` first — \*\*if it is empty, the stamp is yours and  
the stand-off does not apply.\*\* Never treat mtime alone as proof another lane is active on a git-tracked  
file. That is the durable rule; it belongs next to the stand-off rule, not as a replacement for it.  
  
This also means the five earlier cycles that aborted the same merge have been re-stamping \`OPEN-ITEMS.md\`,  
\`PASTE-LOG.md\` and \`RECURRING-ISSUES.md\` roughly every fifteen minutes since the pull order broke. \*\*Any  
"last modified" reading taken off those three files in that window is the abort, not an edit\*\* — do not  
read recency there as activity, and do not date the registry's last real change from it. Signing \`AP-0036\`  
stops the re-stamping as a side effect.

a stale page. The correct move was exactly what 10045 did (refuse to call it lapsed) followed by

\#\#\# A defect I introduced and then repaired in the same cycle  
  
My first pass wrote sidecars for all 16 by ASCII-filtering the raw bytes. For the three HEIC photos  
and the two genuinely-corrupt PDFs that produced \*\*binary garbage — 412 KB, 375 KB and 375 KB of it —  
which would have been indexed as if it were document text and poisoned every future search of this  
corpus.\*\* I caught it on read-back and replaced those five with short triage notes (408–481 bytes)  
recording what the file really is and what it would take to read it. The lesson is the ordinary one:  
a default branch in a type-dispatch loop is where the unhandled cases go to be silently mishandled,  
and file size was the tell — a 375 KB "text" sidecar off a photograph is not plausible.

\#\#\# 1. The 82 Errno-22 rows are one sentence: iCloud Drive is not running  
  
All 82 exist. All 82 carry attribute value \`4199968\` — \`Archive + SparseFile + ReparsePoint + Offline +  
RecallOnDataAccess\`, the signature of a \*\*dehydrated cloud placeholder\*\*. 77 are under  
\`C:\\Users\\Jorge\\iCloudDrive\`, 2 under \`C:\\Users\\JV\\iCloudDrive\`, 3 under \`C:\\Users\\Jorge\\OneDrive\`. Path  
length is not the cause — max 140 characters, none near the 260 limit.  
  
I opened three of them for a 16-byte read. All three returned the same OS error, verbatim:  
  
\> \*\*\`The cloud file provider is not running.\`\*\*  
  
Process check: the only Apple process alive is \`iCloudPasswordsExtensionHelper\`. \*\*There is no iCloud Drive  
provider process on this machine.\*\* So those files have no bytes here to read, and no re-run pass will  
recover them — this is the one item in the residual set that needs a hand, not a script.  
  
\*\*The blast radius is bigger than the 82.\*\* Across the whole \`RUNLOG.tsv\` (22,020 rows), \*\*179 rows touch  
\`iCloudDrive\` and 139 of them errored — a 78% failure rate\*\* against a corpus-wide rate near 8%. iCloud Drive  
is effectively a dead zone in this sweep, and only 40 files there produced text at all.  
  
\*\*And it is not only iCloud.\*\* \`C:\\Users\\Jorge\\OneDrive\\...\` placeholders return the \*same\* "cloud file  
provider is not running" error even though a \`OneDrive.exe\` is alive — because the running OneDrive is signed  
in under the \*\*JV\*\* profile, not the \`Jorge\` one. This sharpens the standing note that \`C:\\Users\\Jorge\` is a  
second profile root: its cloud trees are not merely unswept, they are \*\*unreadable from this session\*\*.

\#\#\# The finding  
  
The OCR sweep is at \*\*\`\[11150/12304\]\`, 1,154 files left\*\*, 4 workers alive, 1,093 files/h. Its error counter  
has been stuck at \*\*\`ERROR: 1016\`\*\* and earlier cycles logged the rising number as a fact about the corpus.  
It is not. It is a fact about the reader.  
  
\*\*843 of the 1,016 error rows — 83% — carry one identical message:\*\* \`TypeError: Unsupported image  
format/type\`. All 843 are image files: 674 \`.jpg\`, 121 \`.heic\`, 47 \`.jpeg\`, 1 \`.heic\`.  
  
I sniffed the first 16 bytes of all 843 rather than trusting the extension. \*\*Every single one is exactly  
what its name says\*\* — 721 real JPEGs (\`FFD8FF\`), 122 real HEIC (\`ftyp/heic\`, one \`heix\`). Zero corrupt,  
zero truncated, zero wrong-extension, zero zero-byte. This is the \*inverse\* of the usual "a corrupt PDF is  
really a mislabelled file" case.  
  
Then I opened 400 of the failing \`.jpg\` files with the same Pillow the sweep uses. \*\*All 400 opened  
cleanly, and all 400 report format label \`MPO\`\*\* — iPhone HDR/burst shots that keep a \`.jpg\` name.  
\`pytesseract\` judges an image by that label, not by its pixels, and \`MPO\` is outside its supported list, so  
it raises \`TypeError\` on a perfectly good photograph. \`pillow\_heif\` is \*\*INSTALLED\*\* on this machine, so the  
122 HEIC would decode too.  
  
\#\#\# Why they still failed — the fix exists and the running process has never seen it  
  
\`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py\` already handles this, at lines 110-141: it compares \`img.format\` against  
pytesseract's supported set and calls \`convert("RGB")\` (which returns a new image with \`.format = None\`,  
treated as PNG) for anything outside it, plus a \`register\_heif\_opener()\` branch for \`.heic\`. The comment  
there even records the same diagnosis from yesterday.  
  
| | |  
|---|---|  
| \`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py\` mtime | \*\*2026-09-01 17:49:46\*\* |  
| running sweep (PID 6332) start | \*\*2026-09-01 16:12:21\*\* |  
  
\*\*The process is 1h 37m older than the fix.\*\* Python read that file once at launch; editing it since has  
changed nothing in flight. This is the same failure already on the board as \*"a fix on disk is not a fix in  
the running process"\* — now measured: \*\*it is costing 843 readable documents, 6.9% of the 12,304-file  
corpus.\*\*

\`C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\\Documents\\Reports\\OCRRUN-10003\_2026-09-01\\CYCLE10043\_TypeError-Sniff.csv\`  
  
\#\#\# What I did NOT do, and the recommendation  
  
\*\*I did not restart the sweep.\*\* Restarting is ask-first, and it would be the wrong move anyway — the run is  
1,154 files from finishing after 10.2 hours. Killing it now to pick up a fix that only affects files it has  
\*already\* passed would trade a live tail for a re-do.  
  
\*\*The right move is a re-run pass, not a restart:\*\* let the current sweep finish (\~63 min at the observed  
rate), then run the \*current\* script over just the 843 paths in that CSV. They need no PDF rendering and no  
page loop — 843 single images at the sweep's own rate is well under an hour. Expected recovery: 843 of 1,016  
errors cleared, residual error count \~173.  
  
The remaining 173 are a different question and are \*\*not\*\* claimed as recoverable here: 82 \`OSError \[Errno  
22\] Invalid argument\`, 44 \`PermissionError \[Errno 13\]\`, 57 \`FileDataError\`, 36 \`EmptyFileError\`, 5 not on  
disk, 5 \`UnidentifiedImageError\`, 3 truncated PDFs, 3 \`DecompressionBombError\`, 3 \`TesseractError\`. The 44  
permission denials and 82 Errno-22 rows smell like cloud-placeholder / long-path reads rather than damage,  
but I have not measured them and will not say so as fact.  
  
\*\*A note on \`ERRORS.tsv\`'s shape — and a correction to my own first draft of this paragraph.\*\* I nearly  
filed the memory index as wrong for saying \*"PATH IS FIELD 1."\* It is not wrong: it is \*\*0-indexed\*\*, and  
the detailed note spells that out — \*"field 0 is the literal tag \`ERROR\` — the path is field 1."\* Both  
readings describe the same file. Stated once without ambiguity: \*\*three tab-separated fields, no header;  
\`\[0\]\` is the literal string \`ERROR\`, \`\[1\]\` is the path, \`\[2\]\` is the reason.\*\* Splitting and taking \`\[0\]\`  
gives you \`ERROR\` for every row. (1,081 rows, 1,022 distinct paths — 59 paths appear twice.) \*\*No change is  
needed to any code or memory that already follows the index.\*\*  
  
Nothing here needs Jorge's hands tonight.

\#\#\# Why  
  
\`C:\\AI\\scripts\\MatterStage\\Finisher-01-Sweep.ps1\`, lines 69–85 and 115–123. When an evidence string is  
not a fully-qualified path, the gate resolves it by a \*\*one-level \`Join-Path\` against a fixed list of  
15 base folders\*\*. It never recurses. Four of the five files sit one to four levels \*below\* a listed  
base — \`Reports\\Undo\_Manifests\\\`, \`ClaudeMemory\\Dictation\\\`, \`PERM-APP-PORTAL\\...\` — so the join lands  
on a path that was never going to exist. The fifth has no base at all: \*\*\`C:\\Users\\JV\\JV-repository\\\`  
is not in the list\*\*, and \`C:\\Users\\JV\\\` + \`mailbox\\to-desktop\\\` is not where the repo keeps it.  
  
The damage is in what happens next. Line 137 is unconditional:  
  
\`\`\`  
$missing = @($resolved | Where-Object { -not $\_.Exists })  
if ($missing.Count -gt 0) {  
 $it.Proven = 'PATH-MISSING' \# hard failure: it names a file that is not there  
 $it.OpenState = 'DONE-UNPROVEN'; $doneUnproven++  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*A base-list miss and a genuinely deleted artifact produce the identical verdict\*\*, and that verdict  
reopens the directive. The script's own comment — \*"it names a file that is not there"\* — is the claim  
it cannot support: it never knew where to look. \*\*A guessed path fails toward a confident ABSENT\*\*, and  
here the confident ABSENT is loud enough to un-close finished work and push it back toward the owner.  
  
Note the shape: the gate exists to catch fake closes. It is itself producing fake failures, at 28%. A  
control that cries wolf on more than a quarter of honest rows is training the next reader to skim the  
section — which is precisely how a \*real\* missing artifact would get waved through.

\#\#\# The premise needed correcting before anything else  
  
The job opened on "a task that reports success while achieving nothing." Right, but not for the assumed  
reason. \`1PW-Migration-Reconcile.ps1\` is \*\*111 lines with no write verb of any kind\*\*. Its only two  
1Password calls are \`op account list\` and \`op item list\`. There is no \`op item create\`, no \`op item edit\`,  
no import. \*\*It is a reporter that was named a reconciler.\*\* It was never going to migrate anything.  
  
And the page it wrote on its last run already said \*\*INCOMPLETE\*\*, and named both vaults. \*\*The lie is not  
in the page — it is in the green light.\*\* \`LastTaskResult = 0\` has been read as "the migration is  
succeeding." It means "the script reached its last line."  
  
\#\#\# Why it can never report anything but 0  
  
Two lines. \*\*Line 11\*\*, \`$ErrorActionPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'\`, swallows every non-terminating  
error. And \*\*line 111 is the last line of the file — there is no \`exit\` statement anywhere in the script.\*\*  
Under \`powershell.exe -File\` that is exit 0, always. The do-nothing path is lines 59–65: when the vault  
can't be read the script prints one sentence, falls through to the verdict, writes its page, and ends  
green. \*\*The one measurement that would prove the migration worked is the one allowed to fail silently.\*\*  
  
\#\#\# The worse defect — it is armed to disable itself on evidence that proves nothing  
  
\`\`\`  
42 $loaded = $stores | Where-Object { $\_.KB -gt 45 } \# browser file SIZES only  
67 $vaultReadable = $true \# set here, NEVER READ AGAIN  
91 if (-not $loaded) { Say "Migration COMPLETE..."; Disable-ScheduledTask ... }  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*The verdict "COMPLETE" is decided entirely by browser-side file sizes. 1Password is never consulted.\*\*  
\`$vaultReadable\` is computed and thrown away. The day the browser stores drop under 45 KB for any reason —  
a profile reset, a Chrome re-sign-in, a fresh \`Login Data\` after an export — the script announces  
\*"Migration COMPLETE. 1Password is the only keeper"\* and \*\*disables its own scheduled task\*\*, with no  
requirement that the vault ever held one item. \*\*A self-disable gated on the absence of the wrong  
evidence.\*\* This is the same shape as the controls whose subject is absent: it cannot fail, so it cannot  
warn.  
  
\#\#\# The mislabel that hid this for weeks  
  
Measured tonight, with timeouts:  
  
\`\`\`  
op account list -\> exit 0, my.1password.com / jorgev2121@gmail.com / 4FYGTC2EG5FMPHKR5BPUUFLRH4  
op item list --format json -\> NO RESPONSE, killed at 45 s  
\`\`\`  
  
\*\*The account IS signed in. The vault is LOCKED.\*\* Line 60 of the script prints \*"1Password CLI is not  
signed in"\* — it cannot tell "not signed in" from "signed in but locked," and it has been printing the  
wrong one. The page has been blaming a sign-in that was never the problem. \*\*A diagnostic that names the  
wrong cause is worse than one that says UNKNOWN\*\*, because it closes the question.  
  
The timing corroborates it: task started \*\*07:35:35\*\*, page written \*\*07:45:02\*\* — \*\*9 min 27 s\*\* for a  
script that does four file stats. Nearly all of it is spent inside \`op\`, hanging, then failing.

I wrote the helper script as UTF-8 \*\*without a BOM\*\* from PowerShell 7, then executed it with  
\`powershell.exe\` \*\*5.1\*\*, which reads a BOM-less file as ANSI. The em-dash in \`01-JOBS — ONE SOURCE OF  
TRUTH\` decoded to \`â€”\`, and the script created and wrote into:  
  
\`\`\`  
G:\\My Drive\\01-JOBS â€” ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH\\  
\`\`\`  
  
This is the \*\*same ANSI double-decode already on this board for \`TO-CLOUD.md\`\*\*, one layer over: there it  
corrupts the \*content\*, here it corrupts the \*path\*. I moved all four files into the real capsule and  
re-verified them there.  
  
\*\*The part that is not about me:\*\* that stray root \*\*already held empty capsule folders\*\* for  
\`TRK-2026-1292\`, \`TRK-2026-1536\`, \`TRK-TBD 535 NW 7 ST (Renzo Cahuana)\` and \`OPH-2026-0007\` before tonight.  
\*\*More than one script on this machine has been writing into the corrupted twin of the jobs root — and each  
one would have reported success.\*\* It holds no files now. It should not exist, and deleting it is Jorge's  
call, so it stands.  
  
\*\*Two rules out of it.\*\* Any script handed to 5.1 whose path contains a non-ASCII character must be written  
\*\*with a BOM\*\*, or the path passed as a parameter instead of embedded. And \*\*a \`SAVED\` line with a byte  
count is not proof — re-list the destination directory.\*\* That is the only thing that caught this.

copies (one from the HEVC batch, one from \`Converted\_HEIC\`). The queue handed both to different workers three

whole run: \*\*\`11785 SW 183 ST - Heating permit final 2-14-2018 - Eugenia Marrero.pdf\`\*\* → \*\*TRK-2026-1265  
(9601 Collins Ave), score 53\*\*, on \`NAME approved,extension,final,phone,process\` + \`UNIT S\` +  
\`EMBED cos=0.70\`. No address hit, no folio hit, no permit hit. \*\*The score is a phantom unit and five  
generic English words\*\* — and those words come from the anchor's own prose, because 1265's anchor is built  
from a capsule title that is a whole status paragraph (63 words including \*final, phone, open, money, real,  
wrong\*). Any document containing "final" and "phone" scores against Bal Harbour.  
  
\*\*THE SECOND-ORDER RISK — THIS CAN DISARM THE WRONG-UNIT GUARD.\*\* Line 287 raises \`UNIT-CONFLICT\` only when  
document units and job units \*\*fail\*\* to intersect. A document containing the word "units" gets a phantom  
\`S\`; a job whose title contains "units" gets a phantom \`S\`; they intersect, \`\\\` is non-empty, and  
\*\*the multi-unit building protection never fires\*\* — on exactly the condo matters where it is the only thing  
between a document and the wrong apartment. \`Apply-Matches.ps1\` is armed. Stated as a mechanism; it was not  
observed firing this run.  
  
\*\*SCOPE, NOT OVERCLAIMED.\*\* Only \*\*2 of 100\*\* anchors carry a phantom unit, and only \*\*2 of 100\*\*  
(1265, 1531) have permit-like title text the permit extractor took nothing from. Sharp defect, small  
blast radius. It does \*\*not\*\* by itself explain 960 runs of zero filings.  
  
\*\*THE FIX — ONE LINE, NOT APPLIED.\*\* \`\\ = '\\bunits?\\s\*\#?\\s\*(\[0-9\]\[\\w-\]{0,7})\\b'\` — require a leading  
digit (kills \`s\`/\`PIPELI\`/\`UNPERM\`), allow a hyphen inside (keeps \`15-20a\` whole), anchor the word.

\#\# 2026-09-01 18:35 — CYCLE 10026 — LAYER 3 NOW RUNS FOR THE FIRST TIME: A 15-SECOND TIMEOUT WAS KILLING IT ON CALL ONE, AND THE LISTING GUARD LANDED FIRST  
  
\*\*Layer 3 of the orphan matcher has never once run. I found the exact mechanism in a log written  
three minutes before I looked, fixed it, and it now runs. But the honest headline is the second  
half: restoring it produced ZERO new filings. It lifts every document by about the same 9 points  
instead of separating the right job from the wrong one — and it feeds a mover that is ARMED.\*\*  
  
\*\*THE MECHANISM, FROM THE LOG, NOT INFERRED.\*\* \`OrphanMatcher\_2026-09-01\_1809.log\`:  
  
\`\`\`  
18:09:41 PM Loaded 100 job anchor records from JobAnchors.json  
18:09:56 PM Ollama unreachable ... Layer 3 scores 0 for this run. Detail: The operation has timed out  
18:09:57 PM Found 44 candidate documents in C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\\Desktop\\Trey List  
\`\`\`  
  
Exactly \*\*15 seconds\*\*, matching \`-TimeoutSec 15\` on line 149. The first job embedding times out,  
the \`catch\` latches \`$script:OllamaDown = $true\`, and the \`break\` on line 183 leaves the pre-compute  
loop with \*\*zero of 100\*\* job embeddings. Every document then scores \`l3 = 0\` against every job. The  
reachable ceiling was 55 + 25 = \*\*80\*\*, and AUTO-FILE needs 85 — so \*\*no document could ever be  
filed, by arithmetic.\*\* One 15-second constant disabled a whole layer and the feature it gates.  
  
Measured on this machine at 18:14 under load (4 OCR workers): cold start \*\*10.3s\*\*, warm \*\*3.5–5.0s\*\*;  
a previously recorded cold start hit 29s. 15s was inside the failure band. Now \*\*120s, and a single  
timeout retries once instead of latching the entire run off.\*\*  
  
\*\*THE LISTING GUARD WENT IN FIRST, AND IT WAS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A NICETY.\*\* The prior run's top  
score was \*\*80 — CONFIRM — \`contents-list.txt\`\*\* against TRK-2026-1451 on  
"PERMIT B26000013 + ADDRESS 10000 W BAY HARBOR DR". The next-highest document scored 40. That file  
is a machine-generated inventory of a cleanup move ("Total moved: 156 items", rows of \`\[DIR \] Name\`).  
It belongs to no job, and it is worse than one wrong match: \*\*the same file also names the addresses  
of TRK-2026-1448 and TRK-2026-1442\*\*, and \`10000 W BAY HARBOR DR\` is an addrkey already known to be  
shared by five capsules. At 80 it was one Layer-3 lift (+19 available) from \*\*99 and AUTO-FILE\*\*.  
  
\`Test-IsFolderListing\` detects inventory row shapes (\`\[DIR \]\`/\`\[FILE\]\`, \`\<DIR\>\`, PowerShell mode  
columns, \`tree\` branches) and fires only at \*\*\>=20 such rows AND \>=30% of non-blank lines\*\*. It only  
ever DOWNGRADES to ORPHAN — it can never cause a file to be filed. Tested on real files:  
\*\*contents-list.txt caught; 0 false positives across the 29 other text documents in the pool.\*\*  
  
\*\*VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT, ON BOTH POOLS.\*\*  
  
| | MESS-TO-BE-REVIEWED | Trey List |  
|---|---|---|  
| Job embeddings built | \*\*100 of 100\*\* (was 0) | \*\*100 of 100\*\* (was 0) |  
| Documents scored | 40 | 34 |  
| Docs that got an EMBED score | 34 | — |  
| AUTO-FILE | \*\*0\*\* | \*\*0\*\* |  
| CONFIRM | 0 | 1 (score 65) |  
| Rows \>= 85 | \*\*0\*\* | \*\*0\*\* |  
  
\*\*THE RESULT IS HONEST AND IT IS NOT A WIN.\*\* Across the 34 documents present in both runs the fix  
raised scores by an average of \*\*+8.6\*\* (max +13) — and \*\*nothing crossed 60.\*\* The reason is in the  
cosine distribution: \*\*min 0.40, max 0.70, mean 0.57\*\*, the entire population inside a 0.30-wide band.  
A red-light speeding ticket scores 0.61 against a job; the single best-matched document scores 0.70.  
\*\*Layer 3 as configured is a floor-raiser, not a discriminator\*\* — roughly 11 points to everything,  
with only about +/-3 points separating the most from the least related document.  
  
\*\*THE HAZARD I CREATED, AND WHY IT IS CURRENTLY CONTAINED.\*\* \`Run-OrphanMatcher.ps1\` calls  
\`Apply-Matches.ps1\` \*\*without \`-WhatIf\`\*\* — it is live and it \`Move-Item\`s every row with  
\`Verdict = AUTO-FILE -and Score \>= 85\`. I have just added \~9 points to every document feeding it.  
I did not assume that was safe: I ran \*\*both\*\* pools and confirmed \*\*0 rows at or above 85\*\*, so the  
armed 18:35 run moves nothing. \`CU-Orphan-Matcher\` is Ready, 30-minute repetition, ExecutionTimeLimit  
PT1H, \`IgnoreNew\`; the new runtime is \~7 min per pool (\~14 min per cycle), well inside both.  
  
\*\*TWO PROPOSALS — NOT ACTIONS, FOR THE BOARD/OWNER.\*\*  
1\. \*\*Do not let a non-discriminative layer approach an armed threshold.\*\* Either score Layer 3 only  
 above a noise floor (rescale cos 0.55–0.75 onto 0–19, so the mean contributes \~2 rather than \~11),  
 or require a Layer 1 hard anchor (folio or permit) before AUTO-FILE is permitted at all. I did not  
 change scoring policy on the evidence of one 40-document pool — that is a decision, not a bug fix.  
2\. \*\*Cache the job embeddings.\*\* All 100 are recomputed from scratch per pool per run — about 4  
 minutes of Ollama every 30 minutes, forever, for a \`JobAnchors.json\` that rarely changes. Key the  
 cache on that file's hash.  
  
\*\*BACKUP AND ROLLBACK.\*\* \`Match-Orphans.ps1.bak-20260901-1815-pre10026\` (17,914 bytes).  
Undo in one command:  
\`Copy-Item 'C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\\Scripts\\OrphanMatcher\\Match-Orphans.ps1.bak-20260901-1815-pre10026' 'C:\\Users\\JV\\OneDrive\\Scripts\\OrphanMatcher\\Match-Orphans.ps1' -Force\`

\#\# 2026-09-01 17:57 — CYCLE 10025 — THE OCR SWEEP THROWS AWAY EVERY IPHONE PHOTO BECAUSE PYTESSERACT JUDGES AN IMAGE BY ITS FORMAT LABEL  
  
\*\*One result, and it is a fix. 46 of the sweep's 147 error rows — 31% — are one bug, and it is not  
a bad file, a locked file or a slow file. Pillow opens these images perfectly. \`pytesseract\` then  
refuses them on the strength of a text label and the page is discarded. One of the discarded pages  
is a Miami-Dade Property Appraiser building-sketch card for folio 30-2124-005-1170; another is a  
Miami-Dade code-compliance case history for a live job address. Fixed and verified on real files.\*\*  
  
\*\*THE MECHANISM.\*\* \`pytesseract.prepare()\` reads \`image.format\` and raises  
\`TypeError: Unsupported image format/type\` unless the label is one of BMP, GIF, JPEG, JPEG2000,  
PBM, PGM, PNG, PPM, TIFF, WEBP. The iPhone produces two labels outside that list and both decode  
fine in Pillow:  
  
| Label | What it is | Failed so far | In the 22,875-file universe |  
|---|---|---|---|  
| \`HEIF\` | \`.heic\` — the default iPhone photo since iOS 11 | 37 | \*\*160 \`.heic\`, so \~123 not yet reached and all of them would have failed\*\* |  
| \`MPO\` | HDR / burst shots that still carry a plain \`.jpg\` name | 9 | unknown — hides inside 3,768 \`.jpg\` + 424 \`.jpeg\`, indistinguishable by filename |  
  
\*\*The script already had a HEIC guard and the guard is not the problem.\*\* \`do\_image()\` tries  
\`import pillow\_heif\` and returns \`SKIP\_HEIC\` if it is absent. \`pillow\_heif\` \*\*1.3.0 is installed\*\*,  
the import succeeds, \`register\_heif\_opener()\` runs, and \`Image.open()\` returns a clean  
3024 x 4032 RGB image. The guard's \`except\` never fires. The failure is one line later, and it is  
about the label, not the pixels.  
  
\*\*MY OWN FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE PRODUCED A USELESS FIX.\*\* I asked \`py -3\` whether  
\`pillow\_heif\` was installed and got \*\*False\*\*. \`py -3\` on this machine is  
\`C:\\Users\\JV\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Python\\Python313\\python.exe\`. The sweep runs under  
\`C:\\Program Files\\Python312\\python.exe\`, where it is \*\*True\*\*. Acting on the first answer would  
have meant "install pillow-heif" — a fix that gains exactly zero, because it is already there.  
\*\*Read the running process's \`ExecutablePath\` and probe THAT interpreter. A launcher alias is not  
the interpreter your job is using.\*\*  
  
\*\*THE FIX.\*\* \`do\_image()\` now normalises only images whose label is outside pytesseract's list:  
\`if img.format and img.format not in SUPPORTED\_FORMATS: img = img.convert("RGB")\`. \`convert()\`  
returns a new image with \`.format = None\`, which pytesseract then treats as PNG. The HEIF opener is  
also now registered for \`.heif\` and \`.hif\`, not just \`.heic\`. \*\*The \~12,000 files that already OCR  
take a byte-identical path\*\* — the branch cannot fire on them.  
  
\*\*VERIFIED ON REAL FILES, NOT ASSERTED.\*\* Compile-checked under the sweep's own interpreter  
(\`py\_compile\`, exit 0), then the patched \`do\_image()\` was called directly:  
  
\- \`77FD3DC4-…HEIC\` → \*\*1,017 chars\*\*: \*"Miami-Dade County Office of the Property Appraiser …  
 Building Sketch Viewer … Folio 30-2124-005-1170 … Living Area 4,995 … Address 240 N 48 ST"\*  
\- \`683575676.jpg\` (MPO, inside \`20965 SW 236 ST - Cesar\`) → \*\*516 chars\*\*: \*"Activities History  
 for Case Number 20200204389"\* — a county code-compliance record on a job folder  
\- \`77540400045\_\_B9C3…JPG\` (MPO, inside the TRK-2026-1582 Plaza reconciliation) → 374 chars  
\- \*\*Controls\*\* — three PNGs that already succeeded in this run re-ran through the patched function  
 unchanged: 3,749 / 3,043 / 1,898 chars. No regression.  
  
\*\*THE 44 \`PermissionError\` ROWS ARE NOTHING AND SHOULD NOT BE CHASED.\*\* All 44 are Windows account  
profile pictures under \`C:\\Users\\Public\\AccountPictures\` — \`{GUID}-Image192.jpg\` and friends. Zero  
business content. The sweep is right to skip them. The remaining errors are 24 \`EmptyFileError\`,  
18 \`FileDataError\` (truncated PDFs), 4 \`UnidentifiedImageError\` (two AppleDouble \`.\_\` stubs),  
3 \`OSError\`, 2 \`DecompressionBombError\`, 1 \`TesseractError\` (the site photo 10024 killed).  
  
\*\*THE HONEST LIMIT — SAME AS YESTERDAY'S TIMEOUT FIX.\*\* The running sweep loaded this module at  
16:13 and will run the old code to the end. \*\*A file edit is not a running configuration.\*\*  
Recovery is free and needs no new machinery: \`process()\` already returns \`ALREADY\` for any file  
that has a sidecar, and failed files have none, so simply re-running the sweep against the same  
denominator retries exactly the failures and nothing else.  
  
\*\*SWEEP HEALTH, MEASURED 17:56.\*\* 13,098 / 22,875 (\*\*57.26%\*\*), progress file stamped 17:56:40,  
parent PID 6332 with four workers all burning (271 / 706 / 743 / 724 CPU-seconds). Every tesseract  
grandchild was seconds old — no repeat of the 61-minute wedge. No ETA published, per 10024.  
  
\*\*THE ORDERED \`git pull\` STARTED A REAL MERGE AGAIN.\*\* \`git pull origin claude/chaude-code-max20-kp2o46\`

minutes, because \`pytesseract.image\_to\_string()\` is called with no \`timeout=\`. I killed that one  
tesseract child, the worker resumed inside 15 seconds, and I added the missing timeout to the  
script so it cannot happen again.\*\*  
  
\*\*A ONE-FILE STALL IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY HEALTHY-LOOKING PROBE.\*\* Cycle 10023 measured the four  
workers' CPU deltas as 0.00 / 3.00 / 3.31 / 3.47 and called the sweep healthy. It \*was\* healthy —  
but that leading 0.00 was not a worker between files, it was a worker that had been blocked for  
an hour and would have stayed blocked. The blocked worker's own CPU reads \~0 because the burn is  
in its tesseract grandchild (PID 39024, 1,924 CPU-seconds, parent 31884). \*\*A worker reading 0.00  
is either idle for a moment or wedged forever, and the parent's CPU cannot tell you which. Read  
the grandchild's start time.\*\* 39024 started 16:13:40 and was still going at 17:15.  
  
\*\*THE FILE.\*\* \`C:\\Users\\JV\\Dropbox\\Transfer 07082025 gks\\...\\\_3630 Battersea Rd FL 33133 - George -  
Elec Permit - City of Miami\\\_Pics of site...\\3630 Battersea Rd - George-53.JPG\` — 4032 x 3024, a  
plain phone photo of a job site, 2.9 MB. Tesseract should read that in seconds. Its layout analysis  
blew up instead. It is now the single ERROR row in \`ERRORS.tsv\` (\`TesseractError: (4294967295, '')\`)  
and can be retried alone later; it is a site photo, so its OCR value is near zero either way.  
  
\*\*THE COST, MEASURED — 1.9% OF FILES ATE 39% OF THE MACHINE.\*\* Parsing all 12,147 \`RUNLOG.tsv\` rows:  
236 files ran over 120 s and consumed 80,593 of 206,436 total worker-seconds. 55 ran over 300 s,  
21 over 600 s. The worst are multi-page plan sheets (\`2340 SW 8 ST Plan BD17014895001B001.pdf\`,

\*\*THE FIX, AND ITS HONEST LIMIT.\*\* \`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py\` now defines \`PER\_IMAGE\_TIMEOUT = 180\` and  
passes it at both \`image\_to\_string()\` call sites (the per-PDF-page path and the whole-image path).  
On timeout pytesseract raises \`RuntimeError\`, which \`process()\` already catches — it becomes an  
ERROR row and the worker moves to the next file. Backup at \`Run-OCRSweep-9754.py.bak-20260901\`;  
the file was compile-checked (\`py\_compile\`, exit 0) and the installed pytesseract was confirmed to  
actually accept a \`timeout\` parameter before I trusted the edit. \*\*This does NOT protect the run  
happening right now\*\* — that process loaded the old module at 16:12 and will keep running it to the  
end. It takes effect on the next run, or on any worker the pool respawns. A file edit is not a  
running configuration.
